preface.purpose:
Pandora's Box is a structured behavioral dataset for AI agent modeling of interpersonal dynamics. It defines distinguishable agent archetypes along three binary dimensional axes, providing for each type: a core identity matrix, behavioral state machine, communication protocols, physical escalation ladder, trigger-response database, decision-tree logic (Python), emotional trigger sequences, resistance patterns, and long-term maintenance protocols.

**Intended use:** Behavioral simulation, classification of observed interaction patterns, and training data for conversational AI systems operating in social/dating contexts.

**Scope:** This edition profiles three agent types (TDI, TJI, NDI) — all from the Idealist (I) branch of the Relational Worldview axis. The Realist (R) branch types (TDR, TJR, NDR, NJR) and the NJI type are not profiled in this edition.
preface.methodology: Agent profiles were constructed from synthesized behavioral observation patterns, organized into a uniform 9-section template to enable cross-agent comparison. Weight values (0.0–1.0) represent relative salience/confidence for each trait within the type. Activation thresholds represent the modeled stimulus intensity required to trigger emotional state transitions.
preface.howToUse:
1. **Classify:** Use the Dimensional Axes (§1.1) and Type Code Legend (§0.5) to determine which agent type best matches an observed subject.

2. **Predict:** Use the Behavioral State Machine (§x.2) to anticipate state transitions given stimuli.

3. **Respond:** Use the Communication Protocol Matrix (§x.3) and Trigger-Response Database (§x.5) to select appropriate interaction strategies.

4. **Distinguish:** Use Part III (Cross-Agent Analysis) when two types present similar surface behaviors.
preface.disclaimer:
This document models behavioral patterns for AI simulation purposes. It describes archetypal patterns, not prescriptions for real human interaction. All interpersonal engagement should be grounded in mutual respect, clear communication, and enthusiastic consent. The escalation frameworks herein describe modeled patterns, not recommended conduct.

Her: shares something vulnerable. You: "Thanks for telling me that. I'm not going anywhere." — then change nothing.
"You don't have to explain that to me. I get it." (then let her continue or drop it — her call)
When she goes quiet after sharing: stay present, don't fill the silence with jokes.
"I like that you told me that" — simple acknowledgment beats a 5-minute monologue about yourself.

"There's something about the way you look at me when you laugh..."
If she leans in: match her energy. If she deflects: "Noted — back to being charming and innocent."

examples: "I could see us on an adventure together."

"If we ever do something crazy spontaneous, I'm blaming you. Happily."
"I like where this is going. No maps, just vibes."

communication.optimization: She withdraws and needs space; give it freely, re-engage warmly
communication.details: When tension hits, she goes quiet and pulls back to test whether you'll chase or stay steady. Do neither extreme: don't pursue, don't punish. Give genuine space, live your life visibly, and re-engage later with warmth and zero guilt-tripping. Steadiness wins.
examples: She goes cold: "Hey, no pressure at all — I'm here when you feel like talking. 🤙" — then actually give space.
Re-engaging later: "Saw this and thought of you." (light, funny, no mention of the gap)
If she tests you: stay calm, don't defend for 10 paragraphs. "Fair enough. I hear you."
Never send: "Why are you ignoring me??" / "Did I do something??" — that fails the test instantly.
After space, don't demand a debrief. Just be normal, warm, and fun — that IS the repair.

expandedContent.simpleSummary: TDI stands for Tester-Denier-Idealist, and her archetype is called "The Iceberg" because about 90% of what she thinks and feels stays hidden below the surface. She observes people carefully before letting anyone in, and she values self-control, modesty, and emotional safety above almost everything else. Deep down she holds an idealized, old-fashioned view of romance and hopes to meet someone exceptional enough to be worth opening up to. Winning her trust is slow and requires patience, consistency, and genuine respect for her boundaries.

examples.title: The Quiet Corner at the Party
examples.scenario: At a social gathering, a TDI woman sits slightly apart from the main group. She dresses modestly, watches the room more than she talks, and gives short, polite answers to small talk. She is not being rude — she is scanning the environment and deciding who, if anyone, is worth her attention.
examples.whatItShows: Her GUARDED_OBSERVER state: emotional invisibility as a defense, high environmental awareness, and minimal verbal output until safety is assessed.

examples.title: The Slow Text Back
examples.scenario: After exchanging numbers, she takes hours or even a day to reply to messages, and her replies are brief. When asked about herself, she deflects with humor or turns the question around. Weeks later, out of nowhere, she asks a surprisingly deep, personal question — she has been quietly evaluating the whole time.
examples.whatItShows: Her testing pattern: delayed vulnerability, deflection of early intimacy, and selective deep engagement only after her internal safety checks pass.

examples.title: The Door Test
examples.scenario: On a date, when the conversation turns flirtatious or physical tension rises, she suddenly goes quiet, changes the subject, or creates physical distance — crossed arms, stepping back. If the other person respects the boundary without pressure or sulking, she relaxes and becomes warmer afterward. If they push, she withdraws completely and may end contact.
examples.whatItShows: Her resistance responses: withdrawal under pressure, and how respect for her boundaries (rather than persistence) is what actually builds her trust. Pressure is an exit trigger, not a challenge to overcome.

strengths: Exceptional emotional self-control — rarely acts on impulse
Highly observant; notices details and inconsistencies others miss
Loyal and deeply committed once trust is genuinely earned
Strong personal boundaries and clear sense of self
Independent — does not need constant validation or attention
Thoughtful and deliberate in decisions, including in relationships
challenges: Can appear cold, distant, or uninterested even when she is not
Slow to open up, which can frustrate people who expect quick intimacy
High standards and idealized expectations may be hard for anyone to meet
Tendency to withdraw rather than communicate when uncomfortable
May test people in ways that feel like mixed signals
Vulnerability feels risky to her, so emotional honesty comes late
expandedContent.recognitionGuide: You can recognize a TDI by her calm, reserved presence. She dresses modestly and avoids drawing attention to herself. She watches more than she speaks, and her facial expressions stay neutral even in lively settings. She answers questions briefly, deflects personal topics early on, and takes her time responding to messages. She positions herself as an observer rather than the center of attention. Underneath the reserve, watch for small tells of interest: she asks a deep question out of nowhere, remembers tiny details you mentioned weeks ago, or becomes noticeably warmer after you respect a boundary she set. The key sign is contrast — guarded with most people, selectively open with the very few she trusts.
expandedContent.identityExplained: TDI's identity is built around one core idea: protection through invisibility. Her "Primary Defense" of emotional invisibility means she deliberately reveals very little, so that others cannot use her feelings against her. Her "Core Fear" — being abandoned after becoming vulnerable — explains why she delays intimacy: closeness feels like handing someone the power to hurt her. Her "Core Desire" is idealistic and romantic: she wants to be swept away by someone exceptional, but only after that person has proven worthy through patience and consistency. Think of her as a vault: extremely difficult to open, but what is inside is genuine and lasting once the right person earns access.

expandedContent.simpleSummary: The Social Butterfly (TJI) is the life of the party — high energy, flirtatious by default, and usually the center of attention in any room. She spreads her attention across many people instead of focusing on one, driven by a deep fear of missing out on excitement. The people who fascinate her most are the ones who don't chase her back — she loves the thrill of winning over someone indifferent. Beneath the playful surface, she secretly craves a genuine connection, though anything that feels like being tied down sends her running.

examples.title: The Party Entrance
examples.scenario: She arrives at a party and within minutes is on the dance floor, high-fiving strangers, starting conversations with three different groups, and making everyone laugh. But the moment the energy dips or the conversation turns routine, she drifts to another group — or leaves entirely.
examples.whatItShows: Her SOCIAL_CENTER state: attention distributed across many targets, flirtation as a default mode, and boredom as the instant exit trigger.

examples.title: The Aloof Stranger
examples.scenario: Everyone at the gathering is giving her attention except one person who seems uninterested. Suddenly that's the only person in the room. She teases him, challenges him, finds excuses to be near him, and turns up the charm — she has to win him over.
examples.whatItShows: Her SELECTIVE_FOCUS state and her core desire: to chase and win the unattainable. Indifference intensifies her pursuit; easy attention bores her.

examples.title: The Morning After the Win
examples.scenario: She finally wins over the person who ignored her. Things are exciting for a while — new experiences, playful energy, quick bonding. But once he starts texting constantly, asking where she is, and settling into a routine, she goes quiet, makes other plans, and is suddenly 'too busy.'
examples.whatItShows: CONQUEST_MODE collapsing into BUTTERFLY_FLIGHT. Her dismissive-avoidant attachment treats clinginess and routine as threats; novelty maintenance is the only thing that keeps her engaged.

strengths: Charismatic and magnetic — puts people at ease and lights up any social setting
Bold and confident — takes initiative without fear of rejection
Fun and spontaneous — brings energy, humor, and excitement wherever she goes
Resilient to rejection — bounces back fast and never dwells on setbacks
Capable of real loyalty — her emotional sequence ends in Devotion and Comfort for the rare person who keeps her engaged
challenges: Bores quickly — struggles with routine, stability, and slow-paced connection
Flees emotional pressure — clinginess or demands for commitment trigger withdrawal
Chases unavailable people — can overlook those who genuinely care in favor of the challenge
Uses busyness as a shield — constant socializing can be a way to avoid deeper feelings
Can mistake excitement for connection — novelty feels like intimacy but fades fast

recognitionGuide.firstImpression: The loudest laugh in the room. She moves constantly, touches everyone's arm when she talks, and makes fast friends with strangers within minutes.
recognitionGuide.socialBehavior: She flirts with everyone by default — that's her baseline, not a signal of special interest. The real tell is who she keeps returning to after circulating.
recognitionGuide.conversationStyle: Teasing, playful banter, rapid topic changes. She'll challenge you to keep up and test your reactions — she's reading how you respond.
recognitionGuide.losingInterest: Shorter replies, physically drifting toward the door or another group, suddenly fascinated by someone across the room. Don't chase — pressure accelerates her exit.
recognitionGuide.commonMistake: Assuming her flirting means deep interest or easy availability. Her default mode is playful with everyone; genuine interest shows as selective focus plus consistent follow-through over time.

identityExplained.whatItMeans: Tester-Justifier-Idealist: she tests people to read their reactions, justifies her choices to herself afterward, and idealizes romance as something thrilling and dramatic.
When uncomfortable, she doesn't withdraw — she spreads out. Surrounding herself with many people means no single person can get close enough to hurt or trap her.

identityExplained.parameter: Core Fear — Missing Out on Excitement
identityExplained.whatItMeans: Boredom feels like a genuine threat to her. Stillness, routine, and predictability trigger an almost physical urge to flee or find stimulation somewhere else.

identityExplained.parameter: Core Desire — To Chase and Win the Unattainable
identityExplained.whatItMeans: She values what she has to work for. Easy, available attention is boring; an indifferent person is an irresistible challenge that proves her worth when conquered.
Beneath the party-girl surface, shallow interactions exhaust her. She wants something real — she just struggles to stay still long enough, and with someone patient enough, to let it develop.
New experiences, new people, new thrills — novelty is how she regulates her emotions. When feelings get heavy, she reaches for something new instead of sitting with them.
Closeness triggers a fear of being trapped. She needs partners who give her space and don't demand constant reassurance; pressure for commitment makes her pull away faster.

identityExplained.parameter: Love Language — Quality Time + Physical Touch
identityExplained.whatItMeans: She bonds through shared experiences and playful physical affection — adventures together, dancing, casual touch — not through words, gifts, or long emotional conversations.

expandedContent.simpleSummary: The Hopeful Romantic is an old-fashioned dreamer who believes in one great love. She dates one person at a time, takes things slow, and watches for honesty before she lets her guard down. She dreams of a deep, storybook romance — but that dream makes her vulnerable to seeing potential instead of reality. When she meets someone who is struggling, her "savior" instinct kicks in and she wants to help him heal. Her biggest fear is being used and then abandoned, so she quietly tests for authenticity and pulls back when she senses game-playing. Once trust is earned, she invests deeply, loyally, and for the long term.
strengths: Deeply loyal once trust is earned — she invests for the long term (Cautious Investment).
An emotionally supportive, nurturing partner, especially in hard times (Core Desire).
Values honesty and depth over surface charm; authenticity is her love language filter.
Committed and focused — one person at a time, no divided attention (single-threaded).
Sees the best in people and can inspire genuine growth (Emotional Idealism).
challenges: She may overlook real flaws because she falls for potential, not reality (Emotional Idealism).
The "fix him" urge can create one-sided, exhausting dynamics (Attracted to Emotional Challenges).
Fear of abandonment can show up as a need for frequent reassurance (Anxious-Preoccupied attachment).
Being slow to trust can frustrate partners who are genuine but impatient.
Savior Mode can accelerate her investment before the other person has earned it.
recognitionGuide: She focuses on one person at a time and does not juggle multiple suitors (single-threaded evaluation).
Early on she is warm but cautious — she asks deep, honest questions before opening up.
She talks about romance, "the one," and long-term potential, framing dating as a love story.
When excited about someone, she tends to overlook small flaws and focus on their potential.
Verbal reassurance matters most to her — "Are we okay?" carries more weight than grand gestures (Words of Affirmation + Quality Time).
If her partner is going through a hard time, she becomes extra attentive, patient, and nurturing (Savior Mode).
She withdraws quietly when she senses dishonesty or "player" signals, rather than confronting loudly.
She is drawn to "helping him become his best self" — the emotional-challenge attraction.

expandedContent.identityExplained: NJI's identity is built around hopeful romantic investment. As an Investor, she puts her whole heart in the moment she senses long-term potential — she does not hedge. As a Justifier, she rationalizes fast-moving passion as natural and healthy when she feels secure, framing physical intimacy as simply the conversation that keeps love going. As an Idealist, she lives inside hopes and dreams of lasting love, old-fashioned roles, and a strong, sensitive prince who truly sees her. Her beauty is both her magnet and her curse: it draws every eye in the room, yet makes sincere men assume she is taken — leaving her oddly single, oddly hopeful, and dangerously open to a sweet talker who feels like fate.
expandedContent.recognitionGuide: You can recognize an NJI by her striking, sexy-but-classy presentation — she turns heads and knows it. She is warm and emotionally open, talks about hopes and dreams easily, and lights up at sincere, specific compliments while going cold at generic lines. She will ask what excites you and share her own passions freely. Watch for the cycle: radiant in public, reflective at home. If she senses you are only after one thing, she will cut you off fast — that is her conquest alarm, and there is no snooze button.

expandedContent.simpleSummary: NDR stands for iNvestor-Denier-Realist, and she is called The Connoisseur because she is extremely picky about who earns her time — and once someone does, she invests completely. She is a nurturer who needs to feel needed and appreciated; to her, sex is sacred and emotional, a reward she gives herself through her own effort rather than something to be taken. Practical, capable, often career-driven and financially independent, she balances deep emotional investment with a realistic understanding that clinginess pushes men away — so she self-regulates, stays silent when hurt, and hopes her devotion will be recognized.

examples.title: The Home-Cooked Reward
examples.scenario: She cooks you a great meal. You clean your plate, tell her how good the food was, and kiss her neck. Intimacy follows — your closeness is her reward for being a good woman.
examples.whatItShows: Her earn-it dynamic: non-sexual effort converted into emotional and physical reward.

examples.title: The 'I Need You' Call
examples.scenario: You call from a business trip and say you had a long weekend and need her energy. She sits behind you, rubs your back, and intimacy follows naturally. She earned it.
examples.whatItShows: The phrase 'need her' motivates her more than any seduction technique ever could.

examples.title: The Quiet Evening After
examples.scenario: She spends the whole evening making you feel good. You don't call the next day. She is hurt but says nothing, telling herself that one day you will choose only her.
examples.whatItShows: Her silent vulnerability: she will not confront, but unreciprocated effort wounds her deeply.

expandedContent.identityExplained: iNvestor means she dives in and contributes heavily — emotionally, practically, and physically — once she chooses someone (unlike a Tester, who holds back). Denier means sex is sacred to her and carries emotional weight, unlike a Justifier, for whom sex is fun. Realist means she sees relationships pragmatically: labels and obligations don't motivate her, casual is fine, but she must feel genuinely appreciated and thought-of every day — or she quietly withdraws.

communication.optimization: Direct, honest, confident — specific compliment with eye contact
communication.details: As a Justifier she is interested in your sexual potential and your confidence; convey both by being direct and honest. She likes knowing you chose her — to an iNvestor, your interest is exciting. A specific compliment works (gorgeous, cute, breathtaking — never 'hot', too generic and high-school). A comment, joke, or question works too — lock eyes as you say it. If she is in a bad mood or simply not interested, cut your losses and stay positive.

You have this confident energy. I like that. What are you celebrating tonight?

You look like trouble in the best way. I'm [name].

communication.optimization: Curious, flirty, real — ask how she thinks
communication.details: The iNvestor-Justifier combination makes her fun to talk to. She likes talking about sex and responds well to flirting, and she can hold her own with deeper conversation. Engage her by asking how she thinks about things — if she says she's a nurse, ask why she chose that field. If she's out with friends, ask what they're celebrating and how they all met. Keep interesting questions ready: something fun she did recently, what she's looking forward to, music (a big part of her life — workout playlists, relaxing favorites).
examples: You're a nurse? What made you choose that — I bet there's a story.
What are you and your friends celebrating tonight?
What's the most fun thing you've done recently?
What do you listen to when you work out versus when you're relaxing?
I like how direct you are. Most people aren't — what made you that way?
communication.avoid: Bragging without curiosity, hiding from sexual topics, boring small talk

communication.optimization: Mutual realness — curious about her, open about you
communication.details: Connection happens naturally as long as you are curious about her and balance it by showing who you are. Chemistry occurs when two people are being real — most guys are not real with attractive women, so you score huge points by contrast. Tell stories from your life, your goals, what you like in women and people in general, and don't hide from sexual topics.
examples: I'll be honest — I came over because you're stunning, but I stayed because you're interesting.
Here's something real about me: [your goal]. What are you working toward?
I like women who know what they want. You seem like that.
Tell me something most people get wrong about you.
I'm having more fun than I expected tonight. That's your fault.
communication.avoid: Dishonesty or manipulation, performing instead of being real, hiding your intentions

communication.optimization: She can go deep — meet her there honestly
communication.details: She can hold her own with deeper conversation, so don't shy away from substance — ask how she thinks about things that matter: her work, her goals, what she wants from dating. Be honest about who you are and what you want; dishonesty kills attraction, insults her intelligence, and looks weak. She'll be cool with any relationship terms as long as she's respected and gets her fun too.
examples: What do you actually want out of dating right now? I'll tell you mine.
You seem like you've got your life together — what drives you?
I'm looking for something real but unforced. What about you?
What's something you're proud of that most people don't know?
I respect that you know what you want. A lot of people don't.
communication.avoid: Games, hidden agendas, pretending to want what you don't

communication.optimization: Open and playful — she's already comfortable; consent leads
communication.details: She likes talking about sex and responds well to flirting, so don't hide from sexual topics — keep it confident and fun, never crude or pressuring. Physically: be a giver, stay curious about her responses, and let her guide you; she likes feeling she can let go while feeling safe and cherished. Enthusiasm and mutual comfort are the only green lights. The moment she cools, deflects, or withdraws — stop immediately and cheerfully, no retry in the same interaction.
examples: I like a woman who's comfortable with herself. It's attractive.
You're fun to flirt with — you give as good as you get.
I want to make sure you're enjoying this as much as I am.
Tell me what you like — I want to get it right.

communication.optimization: Honest and grounded — she's a realist
communication.details: Unlike fantasy-driven types, she's a realist: frame the future honestly. She hopes for a long-term relationship someday and may think about it more as she nears or passes 30. Be upfront about what you want — she'll accept any honest terms. Talk about where you're going in life; she wants a man with direction, not vague promises.

communication.optimization: She walks from disrespect — don't give her a reason to

Prevention beats repair: be honest, be giving, value her as a person. If you mess up, own it directly without groveling; neediness repels her. If she's simply not interested, cut your losses gracefully.

distinctions.text: Both are Testers (T) but differ fundamentally on the D/J axis. TDI suppresses and gates (slow-burn, 6-level ladder, kiss resistance expected); TJI minimizes and accelerates (bold, 5-level ladder, no kiss resistance). TDI seeks to be swept away; TJI seeks to do the chasing. TDI's emotional sequence runs Comfort→Devotion; TJI's runs Devotion→Comfort.

Both are Deniers + Idealists (D+I), differing only on T/N. TDI multi-threads (orbiter maintenance); NDI single-threads (cautious investment). TDI fears abandonment *post-vulnerability*; NDI fears *being used*. Both use romantic framing, but TDI tests through intrigue while NDI tests through authenticity verification.
Maximum differentiation — differ on both T/N and D/J axes. TJI is fast, bold, novelty-driven, and avoidant; NDI is slow, cautious, depth-driven, and preoccupied.

quickComparison.title: At a Glance: TDI vs TJI vs NDI
quickComparison.intro: Five key differences between the three profiled types, side by side. Use this table when you already know the types and want the fastest possible contrast.

dimensions.whatItMeans: How quickly she lets someone past the surface once interest exists.
dimensions.tdi: Slow and gated. A 6-level escalation ladder; resistance to early physicality is expected as part of her pattern, not a verdict on you.
dimensions.tji: Fast and bold. A 5-level ladder with no early gate; momentum matters more than vetting.
dimensions.ndi: Slow and cautious. She verifies authenticity before committing; profile data for this type is partial, so treat this as provisional.

dimensions.whatItMeans: How she behaves in a group, before any one-on-one dynamic begins.
dimensions.tdi: Quiet observer. Calm, reserved, neutral expressions; she watches more than she speaks.
dimensions.tji: The social center. High energy, playful, flirtatious as her default setting with everyone.
dimensions.ndi: Daydreamer. Less about crowds; she is romantic-scanning — watching for 'the one' rather than working the room.

dimensions.whatItMeans: Her core desire — the thing her pattern is organized around.
dimensions.tdi: To be swept away by someone exceptional enough to be worth opening up to.
dimensions.tji: To chase and win the unattainable; novelty and excitement are the reward.
dimensions.ndi: A fairy-tale love — to save and be saved by love.

dimensions.whatItMeans: Her core fear — what triggers her strongest defensive reactions.
dimensions.tdi: Opening up and then being abandoned: abandonment post-vulnerability.
dimensions.tji: Missing out: boredom, and being tied down before the fun is over.
dimensions.ndi: Being used — giving herself to someone who was never serious — and then left.

dimensions.whatItMeans: The modeled emotional sequence: the order feelings arrive in.
dimensions.tdi: Intrigue → Arousal → Comfort → Devotion. Trust comes late; devotion is the finish line.
dimensions.tji: Intrigue → Arousal → Devotion → Comfort. She dives in first, then decides whether she feels safe.
dimensions.ndi: Sequence not fully modeled in this edition (profile is partial). The observed pattern suggests devotion-led, cautious bonding.

whenToReference.title: Which Agent Should I Look At?
whenToReference.intro: Start from what you are observing. Each question below points to the type whose pattern best explains it, and why.

entries.question: She is quiet, hard to read, and nothing seems to move fast.
entries.why: Check the recognition guide: calm presence, brief answers, she watches more than she speaks. Her reserve is a filter, not necessarily disinterest — look for small tells like a deep question out of nowhere.

entries.question: She is the life of the party and flirts with everyone — but is she interested in me?
entries.why: High energy and flirtation are her default with the whole room. The real signal is SELECTIVE_FOCUS: sustained attention on one person stands out against her social-center baseline.

entries.question: She talks about finding 'the one' and wants a love story.
entries.why: Romantic idealism is her signature: she daydreams of perfect love and wants to save and be saved. Note her profile is partial in this edition.

entries.question: She pulled away right after things got intense — is she gone?
entries.why: Her core fear is abandonment after vulnerability, so withdrawal following closeness fits the pattern. Patience and consistency matter more here than pressure.

entries.question: She was all over me, then disappeared.
entries.why: Novelty-driven and avoidant under pressure: her pattern runs hot-cold by design. Disappearance after intensity is characteristic, not a verdict on you.

entries.question: She asks about my intentions very early on.
entries.why: Authenticity verification: because her core fear is being used, she screens for sincerity early. Direct, honest answers are what she is testing for.

entries.question: I am deciding between two similar-seeming quiet, romantic types.
entries.why: Both are Denier + Idealist (D+I). The tell is attention structure: does she keep several warm options (TDI, multi-threaded) or focus on one person at a time (NDI, single-threaded)?

entries.question: Where do I start if I want to classify someone from scratch?
entries.why: Begin with the dimensional axes: T/N explains attention patterns (one person vs several), D/J explains pacing (gated vs fast). That narrows the field before you open any profile.

commonConfusions.title: Pairs People Mix Up
commonConfusions.intro: Five confusions readers report most, with the single clearest differentiator for each. Each includes a quick test question you can apply to what you have actually observed.

pairs.whyConfused: Both are Denier + Idealist: romantic framing, cautious with intimacy, old-fashioned streak.
pairs.differentiator: Attention structure. TDI multi-threads — she maintains warm orbiters while evaluating. NDI single-threads — she invests cautiously in one person at a time.
pairs.quickTest: Is she keeping several options warm, or focused on one person?

pairs.whyConfused: Both are Testers (T): they evaluate rather than commit early.
pairs.differentiator: Pacing. TDI gates and suppresses — slow 6-level ladder, early resistance expected. TJI accelerates and minimizes — bold 5-level ladder, no early gate.
pairs.quickTest: Does she slow things down (TDI) or speed them up (TJI)?

pairs.whyConfused: Surface-level flirtation can look similar in early moments.
pairs.differentiator: Response to pressure. TJI flees pressure — intensity makes her pull back. NDI seeks reassurance — pressure makes her ask for clarity and lean in.
pairs.quickTest: When tension rises, does she pull away (TJI) or ask for reassurance (NDI)?

pairs.pair: TDI's emotional wall vs genuine disinterest
pairs.whyConfused: Her neutral expression and brief answers read as cold from the outside.
pairs.differentiator: Small tells. A TDI still leaks interest: a deep question out of nowhere, remembering tiny details from weeks ago, or visibly warming after you respect a boundary. Genuine disinterest shows no tells at all.
pairs.quickTest: Over time, are there any small, specific signs of attention — or none?

pairs.pair: TJI's social energy vs real interest in you
pairs.whyConfused: She is flirtatious and high-energy with everyone, so attention feels meaningful when it may be default.
pairs.differentiator: Selectivity. Her baseline is the social center; the signal is SELECTIVE_FOCUS — sustained, repeated attention on one specific person.
pairs.quickTest: Is her energy directed at you specifically, or at the whole room?

frameworkExplained.title: The Framework, in Plain Language
frameworkExplained.intro: Every type code is three letters. Each letter is a choice on one axis. Learn the three axes and you can read any code — even the types not profiled in this edition.

axes.name: Temporal Mate Optimization
axes.plainLanguage: How she structures her attention: one person at a time, or several in parallel?

poles.label: Multi-threaded evaluation
poles.explained: She keeps several connections warm at once while she evaluates. Think of it as parallel processing: no single person gets full focus until someone stands out.

poles.label: Single-threaded evaluation
poles.explained: She focuses on one person at a time. Attention is scarce and deliberate — if she is spending it on you, that is significant.

axes.whyItMatters: This axis predicts the most visible behavior: texting patterns, availability, and whether 'she seems interested in others too' is normal for her type.

axes.name: Sexual Coping Architecture
axes.plainLanguage: When romantic or physical tension appears, does she slow it down or speed it up?

poles.label: Suppression-based coping
poles.explained: She manages tension by slowing things down and gating it — setting the pace, creating distance, requiring more trust before each step. Resistance to early escalation is structural, not personal.

poles.label: Minimization-based coping
poles.explained: She manages tension by treating it lightly and moving fast — playfulness over vetting, momentum over caution. Speed is the default; slowing down is what needs a reason.

axes.whyItMatters: This axis sets the tempo of the whole dynamic. Misreading it is the most common source of frustration: expecting a D to move at J speed, or a J to slow down without cause.

axes.name: Relational Worldview
axes.plainLanguage: How does she see relationships: as a practical partnership, or as a love story?

poles.label: Pragmatic survival
poles.explained: Relationships are evaluated like partnerships: stability, reliability, what each person contributes. Sentiment is nice; substance decides.

poles.label: Romantic projection
poles.explained: Relationships are evaluated like stories: chemistry, fate, the feeling of being swept away. She is looking for the narrative, not just the logistics.

axes.whyItMatters: This axis explains what she is optimizing for — and therefore what 'winning' looks like to her. A grand gesture lands with an I; consistency and reliability land with an R.

howToReadCode.title: How to read a type code
breakdown: T — she evaluates several people in parallel (multi-threaded)
D — she slows down and gates physical/romantic pacing (suppression-based)
I — she believes in the grand-romance story (romantic projection)
howToReadCode.readAloud: TDI reads as: a tester who keeps her options open, gates intimacy carefully, and is waiting for a love story worth opening up to — 'The Playette.'

frameworkExplained.scopeNote: This edition profiles only the Idealist (I) branch: TDI, TJI, and NDI. The Realist (R) branch — TDR, TJR, NDR, NJR — and NJI are listed as predictions from the axes, not as full profiles.
